say: Do not defend €3 for a checked booking if checking alone exhausts its labour allowance. The unresolved question is whether organisers value independent verification enough to pay more, rather than book directly with suppliers. Test two explicit hypotheses: €3 per completed rental for an introduction only, with suppliers confirming quantities, dates and cleaning terms directly; or €9 per completed rental for one independently checked supplier quote, one clarification round and no dispute handling. Neither price is validated. If charging only the service fee through Stripe at the supplied standard EEA-card rate, €3 leaves about €2.71 and €9 abo

evidence.quote: 1.5% + €0.25 for standard European Economic Area cards

uncertainty: Willingness to choose either paid scope over direct supplier contact; the supplied receipts do not establish demand.
Loaded labour cost, handling time, other variable costs and target contribution needed to justify either proposed fee.
Whether one checked quote without dispute support solves the organiser's actual problem.
dissent: Removing checking may remove the reason to use the service, while raising the fee may make direct supplier booking more attractive. If buyers mainly want accountability when something goes wrong, neither proposed scope is sufficient.

uncertainty: Which properties still require manager-arranged grit and whether their managers qualify for free collection.
Delivered quantities, lead times, collection restrictions and actual supplier delivery costs.
Existing direct-booking alternatives and comparable delivered prices.
Manager willingness to request delivery at a stated total price.
Provider willingness to accept the proposed completion fee.
dissent: A small, seasonal convenience service could be useful even when the material is free; lack of paying customers at planning stage is not itself grounds to drop the hypothesis.
A provider-paid fee might work if requests fit existing routes, but route fit and incremental margin remain untested.
